label: def:three-calibration-discipline
title: Three-calibration discipline ($m_e$, $m_\mu$, $m_\pi$) aligned to (co)homological data
html:
Definition. Three-calibration discipline (m_e, m_\mu, m_\pi) aligned to (co)homological data

The QOU framework admits exactly three external calibration inputs. These are the three real degrees of freedom of the first cohomology of Bring's curve, H^1 = 2W:

DOF of H^1(\text{Bring}) = 2W Canonical observable What it fixes Numerical proxy (source)
W-plane scale (h^0) m_e (leptonic mass scale) the dimensional unit (scale) m_e, CODATA (electron mass)
W-plane modulus (h^2) P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} (neutron \beta-sector bar-skew channel) q_0 via m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}; modulus pinned most precisely by m_\mu/m_e (CODATA muon mass)
orthogonal class (meson sector, h^3) P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi} (pion-sector bar-even channel) the \mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{Hopf})=0 meson scale (independent of m_e, q_0) m_\pi, PDG (charged-pion mass)

For every confined hadronic state X, the mass functional defined by the algebraic-side chain (categorical action, Frobenius pairing, mass identity, mass-endomorphism tower, Jones–Markov trace) factors as

  \mathfrak{m}(X) \;=\;
  m_e^{\,a(X)}\;m_\pi^{\,c(X)}\;Q_X(q_0),
  \qquad
  Q_X(q) \in \mathbb{Q}(q),

with non-negative integer exponents a(X), c(X) determined by the (co)homological grading of the observable X. Concretely: a counts mass-scale insertions (H^0 — the W-plane scale), c counts meson-sector insertions (the orthogonal m_\pi class; c = 0 in the baryon sector), and q_0 is fixed by the lepton ratio m_\mu/m_e (the H^1 W-plane modulus, CAL-2 = P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}). The parameter \mathfrak{Q}_\beta is the CAL-2 proxy. It is the bar-odd (\sinh) partner of the bar-even (\cosh) meson scale m_\pi under the bar-involution q \mapsto q^{-1} (substrate cohomology calibration story). It represents the experimental face of the modulus that CAL-2 pins. It is not a separate dimensional mass-formula factor.
